item.title: Barbara Keating died in the 9/11 attack. She's finally being laid to rest
item.description: Barbara Keating died aboard one of the planes that hijackers slammed into the World Trade Center. Her remains were finally identified last year, and her family is gathering for a long-delayed funeral.
item.content:encoded:
Barbara Keating died aboard one of the planes that hijackers slammed into the World Trade Center. Her remains were finally identified last year, and her family is gathering for a long-delayed funeral.

(Image credit: Family of Barbara Keating, used with permission)

item.title: 'I've never seen anything like this' -- A U.S. doctor treats Ebola's youngest victims
item.description: Dr. Rupa Narra is a U.S. pediatrician who arrived in the Democratic Republic of Congo to help care for stricken children. Nothing could have prepared her for what she'd face.

item.description: Sept. 11 represented a new kind of national security threat, and a new national security architecture was created to confront it.

item.title: Scientists say August was Earth's hottest month they've measured
item.description: The European climate service Copernicus said the Earth just sweltered through its hottest month on record in August. Scientists said the heat surge is mostly due to human-caused climate change.

item.title: A pilot of the Amazon cargo plane in Miami crash warned it was coming in too fast
item.description: For nearly two minutes, one of the pilots of the Amazon cargo plane that careened off a Miami runway repeatedly warned his counterpart they were going too fast, according to flight information.

item.title: After 900 years, the Bayeux Tapestry returns to England and goes on display in London
item.description: The nearly 230-foot long Bayeux Tapestry is back in England for the first time in 900 years. It depicts the 1066 Battle of Hastings, a turning point in English history that ended Anglo-Saxon rule.
